claims.text: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12, 2026.
BRICS member nations signed the New Delhi Declaration 2026, calling for UN Security Council reforms and greater participation of developing economies in global decision-making.
China and Russia reiterated support for the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the United Nations, including its Security Council.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi told President Xi Jinping that peace and tranquility in border areas remain an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations.
PM Narendra Modi met Philippines President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on September 13, 2026, agreeing to expand cooperation in defence, security, trade, and space.
PM Modi held bilateral meetings on the margins of the summit with leaders from South Africa, Kazakhstan, Uganda, Nigeria, and Burundi.
PM Narendra Modi warned against the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals during the final session of the BRICS summit.
The four pillars of India's BRICS chairship were resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability.
India condemned an attack on the Panama-flagged oil tanker MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman on September 13, 2026.
Thirteen Indian crew members of MT El Gaia were rescued, while search and rescue operations continued for one missing Indian seafarer.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed creating a Seafarers' Emergency Support Network during the BRICS summit to safeguard mariners in conflict zones.
Ten Indian seafarers are among 16 Indians killed in the West Asia conflict, while another five Indian seafarers have died in strikes on merchant vessels in the Black Sea.
An Iranian cargo vessel was struck near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on September 13, 2026, leaving one person dead and four injured.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the Strait of Hormuz would be opened on the condition that the United States terminates its blockade.
Indian seafarers account for over 12% of the global merchant shipping workforce, comprising nearly 312,000 of the world's 2.57 million seafarers.
The Indian women's cricket team defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in Dubai to win the Women's Asia Cup on September 13, 2026.
The Indian team refused to collect the trophy from Asian Cricket Council President Mohsin Naqvi, who is also Pakistan's interior minister.
Indian head coach Amol Muzumdar stated that the decision not to accept the trophy from Mohsin Naqvi was taken by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).
The Indian men's cricket team similarly declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi after winning the men's tournament in September 2025.
The victory marked a record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title for the Indian women's cricket team.
Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu accepted the runners-up cheque from Mohsin Naqvi during the presentation ceremony.
Shafali Verma scored 68 runs off 39 balls and Smriti Mandhana scored 59 runs off 39 balls to build a 129-run opening partnership for India.
Indian bowler Shree Charani took four wickets for 20 runs as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 111.
